newsitem.title: CANADA: Mitel shares fall on Q3 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Mitel shares fall on Q3 earnings.

text.p: Mitel Corp shares fell in active trading in Toronto on Friday after the company's third-quarter earnings disappointed some analysts.

The stock had enjoyed a solid run-up in recent sessions. Since mid-month, Mitel shares have risen 1.85 to a new 52-week high of 10.85. On Friday, the stock was down 1 at 9.70 after earlier hitting a session low of 9.55.

"I think there were some analysts out there who had been talking up the story with some earnings estimates in the C$0.13 to C$0.14 (a share) range," said Mark Lawrence, an analyst at Loewen Ondaatje McCutcheon.
Lawrence last week cut his third-quarter estimate to C$0.12 a share. After market close on Thursday, Mitel reported a profit of C$0.10 a share in the period.

Mitel spokesman Ian Chadsey said the lower than expected earnings were due largely to increased research and development and sales, general and administrative costs from the launch of the MediaPath and NeVaDa products last autumn.
"I thought it was a good quarter -- nothing to write home about, but I think the long-term trend is still intact and here down below 10 bucks I think it's a great buying opportunity," Lawrence said.

"The most important thing is that a lot of critics have been saying that the PBX (private branch exchange switch) business is dead and yet they were able to achieve a nearly 20 percent growth in PBX sales in the quarter," Lawrence added.
Mitel's North American PBX market share has grown to 9.3 percent from 8.9 percent last year, Lawrence said.
((Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com))
